_note: Every place Lords2.exe asks for a sound, and what we do about each one.
docs/audio-triggers.md is the prose; this is the counted form of it, and
crates/l2-game/tests/sfx.rs is what stops it rotting.
The `sites` array is GENERATED from the decompilation --- the id, addr,
prim, class and arg columns all come out of `node tools/oracle/sounds.js
are ours. `--check` asserts the two agree in both directions.
reproduced      we fire this trigger; `ours` names the file and there is
a `// sfx: <id>` marker on the line.
blocked         the mechanic behind it is not built. `note` NAMES it.
dead            the shipped game cannot reach it. `note` is the evidence.
missing         nothing above applies --- it is reachable and unwired.
A marker may claim SEVERAL ids, comma-separated, and that is not a fudge:
the sixteen Msg_PlayVoice sites are one ladder with one condition each and
our `voice_tick` is that ladder, so one call site honestly answers all
sixteen. What the check forbids is an id claimed twice.

DEAD IN THE SHIPPED GAME, and docs/bugs.md D38 said so before this file did - it was filed missing here, which is the inventory contradicting the bug list. The guard is DAT_0053F238 == 1 after a bitwise NOT; Battle_Start seeds the word 0xFFFFFFFF and every live writer stores 0, 0xFFFFFFFF or its NOT, so it alternates between 0 and -1. The one writer that could make it 1 is FUN_00434E68 (DAT_0053F238 ^= 1), and that function has zero rel32 calls or jumps and zero absolute references in the image [V]. docs/bugs.md D38.

Director::chain_takes, reached from a tip window crate::tip posts. [V]: one caller, Msg_DrawWindow's categories 0x05..0x09 branch, from timer < 0x780. It reads n = table[group*5 + cursor] at 0x004E1E40 (names::TIP_TAKES, read out of the exe); while Sound_OneShotBusy() it stamps the time, and once more than 999 ms have passed since the last busy stamp it advances the cursor and plays S201_02.wav + (n-1)*0x10 (names::TAKE_POOL). The cursor DAT_0052F004 is reset only in Tip_Show, carried here as Tips::shows. One stated divergence: timeGetTime() becomes the director's tick count at TICK_MS, so 'more than 999 ms' is 63 ticks. This note used to blame the chain for S010_13.wav, which is g_msgVoiceS010's.

The kind-4 arm: Sound_RestartSlot(1) inside the hit test, guarded by g_mouseLeftPressed || g_mouseLeftDoubleClick - the INITIAL press, never the auto-repeat pulses. Press::press is that line; Screen::take_clicks and Machine::clicks carry it to Director::hear_the_click without letting a screen reach Audio (netcode D-3). tests/click.rs asserts the silent cases; tests/audio_wiring.rs that it reaches the mixer.

The kind-5 arm: Sound_RestartSlot(1) on the press, and the handler runs twenty frames later out of the countdown loop, silently. Press::press_delayed is that line, reached both through Press::event and by hand from DiplomacyScreen. tests/click.rs asserts the delayed fire is silent.
